contractAudit.schedulingContract: kanban_schedule parks the owned current run until an orchestrator unblocks it; it creates no timer and cannot bypass a goal-mode completion judge.
contractAudit.note: The pinned module registers fifteen kanban tools; kanban_schedule is outside the literal Hermes core list and remains in the required contract audit. Todo lists and child delegation do not implement dispatcher ownership, compare-and-swap run transitions, review/change states, structured handoffs, dependency routing, scheduling and attachments.

executionContract.pythonVariables: Fresh interpreter on each call; variables do not persist
executionContract.browserAndWorkspace: Named browser session and owned workspace persist across calls
executionContract.toolSelection: Configured browser-use backend replaces the default browser tool surface; availability is checked during schema selection
executionContract.namedSessionIsolation: Shared CDP routes pin named daemons to their own targets; private per-name routes preserve their private browser
executionContract.redaction: Vault-injected values are redacted from model-visible stdout and stderr
executionContract.screenshots: A newly captured screenshot path is resolved to actual native image output
executionContract.desktopControl: Bot Desktop routes use the same human-control lease fence as built-in browser tools

contractAudit.note: Backend-gated Python browser helpers, named daemon/tab isolation, vault-aware output redaction, physical timeout containment and browser-session routing require their own contract verification; existing Python host callbacks are not full parity evidence.
